newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: European Union welcomes Tajikistan peace agreement.
newsitem.headline: European Union welcomes Tajikistan peace agreement.

text.p: The European Union welcomed on Wednesday a peace agreement ending four years of civil war in the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan, and said it hoped the deal would lead to a new era of stability for the country.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri signed a final peace agreement for the Central Asian state last Friday in Moscow.

"The European Union hopes that this agreement will constitute a lasting political settlement of the conflict and will mark the start of a new era of political stability and economic prosperity in the history of Tajikistan," the EU's Luxembourg presidency said in a statement.
It added that the EU would "unreservedly encourage all the parties in Tajikistan to cooperate with the Commission (for) National Reconciliation in implementing the peace agreement".
Under the agreement -- brokered by Russia, Iran and the United Nations -- Rakhmonov remains president but 30 percent of government posts must be given to the opposition.
Nuri will chair the 26-member National Commission for Reconciliation, in which places will be divided equally between each side.
The commission must work out constitutional changes and prepare elections for a new parliament, which must take place before the end of 1998.
